script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 6. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Your attention is finite.  Every notification, every distraction, every wandering thought costs you.  In a world designed to capture your attention, the ability to direct it deliberately is a superpower.

When you switch tasks, part of your attention stays on the previous task—'attention residue.' It takes about 23 minutes to fully re-engage. Every switch costs you. Protect blocks of uninterrupted time for deep work. Willpower is limited; environment is powerful.  Put your phone in another room.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Attention is your most valuable resource.  Focus teaches that where you direct attention determines what you create.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Focus Session - Remove and Concentrate.

Here's your activity: Do one 25-minute focus session today: phone away, notifications off, single task only. Notice how it feels. Notice when your mind wanders. Notice what you accomplish. This is the Pomodoro technique—and it works. This helps you practice deliberate focus.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about paying attention on purpose can be applied to focus session - remove and concentrate. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
